title: Lsp2 links early-life diet to adult translation and lifespan in Drosophila.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the jPOST FTP folder for PXD062930/JPST003763 (158 files, mostly 1.4-13 GB Thermo .raw files plus a 707 GB all-in-one zip). Downloaded and opened sample_info_for_pSILAC.xlsx (60 pulse-SILAC samples: 4 larval whole-body label checks, 56 adult head samples across diet x day x genotype, 4-6 replicates each), report.pg_matrix_Larvae_prepupa_Lsp2RNAi.tsv (9,468 protein groups x 48 runs of plain label-free abundance; UniProt IDs and gene symbols present), and report_pSILAC_samole_01_04_.parquet (78,330 precursor rows, DIA-NN output with a Channel column H/M/L; only the 4 larval check samples).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Data availability statement (from the bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2025.05.18.654697, not the paywalled Nature version): sequencing runs DRR622306-DRR622313 and DRR626770-DRR626793 at DDBJ, proteomics PXD062930, code 'on request'. Lifespan curve data and sample sizes were not seen; no Nature source data was retrievable (no PMCID, publisher pages not scraped). The adult pSILAC precursor reports (report_pSILAC_samole_05_12.parquet, 122.7 MB; report_pSILAC_samole_29_60.parquet, 512 MB) exceed the 50 MB cap and were not opened.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: anonymous FTP at jPOST works; small processed files downloaded without login. Lifespan data not located in any repository.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in files: the only per-item label that is plausible for ML (fraction of each adult head protein still built from larval heavy-labelled lysine/arginine) is not a column. It must be computed from precursor-level DIA-NN channel quantities (H/M/L) across runs, with policy choices on missing channels and peptide-to-protein roll-up. The lifespan outcome is a handful of survival curves, not a table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: UniProt accessions and gene symbols present; sequences would need a one-shot UniProt proteome download (easy).

a4_units_stated.note: Checked: DIA-NN quantities are arbitrary intensity units; a heavy fraction would be unitless.

a5_enough_rows.note: Per-protein: ~9,468 protein groups in the label-free matrix (checked); number with quantified adult heavy channel unknown (adult parquet not opened). Per-condition (diet to lifespan) n is tiny: 2 larval diets x 2 genotypes.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Adult precursor reports total ~635 MB; fits RAM but exceeds the project's 50 MB download cap.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Sample sheet lists 60 pSILAC samples consistent with the design described; paper counts not seen to compare.

a8_label_provenance.note: Heavy fraction would be a direct mass-spectrometry measurement, not a model output.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) would fit a per-protein retention task

integration.partner_dataset: UniProt Drosophila proteome; published fly protein turnover (pulse-SILAC) datasets
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which sequence or abundance properties make a protein carry larval amino acids into adulthood, beyond simply being slow-turnover?

controls.positive_control: Ribosomal proteins and storage proteins (Lsp1/Lsp2) should show high larval-label retention, as the paper reports.
controls.external_validation: None identified with the same larva-to-adult labelling design.

honest_claim_h3: At best: predicts which adult fly head proteins retain larval-derived lysine/arginine at day 3-6 under two larval diets in one strain, which is largely a protein-turnover proxy.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's sequence to predict how much of it, in the adult fly head, is still built from amino acids eaten as a larva.
plain_idea.train_on: Each adult head protein's sequence (and abundance); roughly several thousand proteins, exact count unknown because the adult files exceed the download cap.
plain_idea.predict: The fraction of the protein carrying heavy-isotope lysine/arginine fed only during the larval stage, measured by mass spectrometry; it would have to be computed from peptide-level channel intensities.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would show whether larval nutrient carry-over is a general turnover effect or specific to certain protein classes; but the label is not tabulated and overlaps heavily with protein half-life work.

ml_idea: Per-protein regression of larval-label retention in adult heads from ESM-2 embeddings plus abundance, ePR vs control as a second task. Blocked because the label must be built from 635 MB of precursor-level DIA-NN output and the lifespan outcome has only a few conditions.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: ~5,000 fly proteins through ESM-2 35M on CPU; precursor parquet roll-up in pandas.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Download report_pSILAC_samole_29_60.parquet and count proteins with a quantified heavy channel in at least 4 of 6 replicates per condition.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 (checked in the files): the only usable per-protein label, how much larval heavy-labelled amino acid remains in each adult protein, isn't a column. It has to be built from precursor-level DIA-NN channel intensities in files over the 50 MB cap. The diet-to-lifespan outcome covers only a few conditions, and the per-protein task is mostly a stand-in for protein turnover.
